biography.plain_text: King Fahd bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was Saudi Arabia's fifth monarch, ruling from 1982 until his death in 2005. A son of the kingdom's founder, he rose through education and interior ministries before succession. His reign combined state-led infrastructure growth with the Basic Law of Governance and expansion of the Two Holy Mosques.

long_biography.plain_text:
Education defined King Fahd's first national office. Appointed the kingdom's inaugural education minister in 1953, he planned new educational infrastructure and established King Saud University four years later. The portfolio placed him at the centre of Saudi Arabia's transition from limited formal schooling to a national system.

During Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, Fahd made the consequential decision to admit international coalition forces to Saudi territory. The decision aligned Gulf, Islamic and Western partners around defence of the kingdom and restoration of Kuwait. Saudi territory then became a principal base for the campaign that expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait.
